items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: We did that, and then we did this -- now, we did that month with Ray Copelan, GG and Art Blakie, and Coleman Hawkins and myself.

ctx.x: This was before the monk and train period?
I was just getting in to the monk and train period. See, because we got ready to do Thelonious (unintelligible) that's the one with Coleman Hawkins and ...

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Cole Train was supposed to come in two or three weeks following that; you know, just as singles, to use our rhythm section.

ctx.x: Anyway, we played. It wasn't a good turnout but we got paid; I got paid, you know, Griffin got paid, Phil Thomas got paid and Jody Jerry got paid and, Henry Richard Brown was the walking delegate; walking around with his [twisted] leg, you know, and that knocked the concerts out, because he

Rollins; couldn't contact Sonny Robinson; he was supposed to come in, Coltrane maybe about a week later, or two weeks later, and Cole Train was supposed to come in two or three weeks following that; you know, just as singles, to use our rhythm section. So, that folded.

So I'm stuck in Chicago now, but I'm happy to be home. I got a chance to relax some; I'm staying at his house, and I was kind of babysitting, because they had a little girl there, and when Don and his wife would cut out, I'd sit with the baby and have a few friends over, you know, and that was it. And I wanted to get around and see somebody, and started visiting some of the old guys in the neighborhood; went over to see there was a club called McKee's Chris Anderson and Leo, and (unintelligible) and they'd bring…

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I remember seeing Stan Colemang Hawkins and Ben Webster in the club one night -- that was an experience. ... I didn't talk to him.

ctx.x: But there was a new era coming and all that next

year in '54 -- that was when Johnny Griffin, Clean Head, Junior Mance, Jimmy Matz, Buddy Smith and myself were working for this same guy at the Flame; he had 2 clubs. The Flame and Basin Street -- right there in Chicago. And oh boy, we used to have swinging times. Tune Up, Clean Head's tune; Johnny Griffin playing his butt off -- I remember seeing Stan Colemang Hawkins and Ben Webster in the club one night -- that was an experience.
them, I didn't talk to him. Like I said, I was always shy with those big names.
